articles.headline: Greg Rousseau's sacks, Josh Allen's rushing TDs are on record paces
articles.description: With multiple sacks and rushing TDs, Rousseau and Allen are on cusp of streaks no one else has done.
articles.headlineJa: グレッグ・ルソーのサック数とジョシュ・アレンのランTDが記録的なペースに
articles.descriptionJa: 複数のサックとランTDを記録しているルソーとアレンは、誰も成し遂げたことのない連続記録の目前に迫っている。
articles.body:
ORCHARD PARK, N.Y. -- Buffalo Bills outside linebacker Greg Rousseau has quite literally run out of room in his trophy case.

Coach Joe Brady keeps giving Rousseau game balls for his performances that earned him AFC Defensive Player of the Month, and, given the limited space in Rousseau's modest game room display case, the sixth-year sack artist admits he might need to invest in a bigger one.

Rousseau is on a torrid pace, logging two sacks in each of the Bills' first three games and his total of six leads the NFL. So If Rousseau's having those problems, just imagine the boondoggle quarterback Josh Allen is in.

Like Rousseau, Allen's out to a blazing start, leading MVP discussions with not only five passing touchdowns but six rushing touchdowns too, two in each game.

With two rushing touchdowns in Week 4 against the New England Patriots on Sunday (1 p.m. ET, CBS), Allen would be the first player in NFL history -- regardless of position -- to punch in multiple touchdowns in four straight games to start a season. He's already in rarified company by even doing so in his first three games; only Priest Holmes (2003), Stephen Davis (1999) and Hall of Famer Jim Brown (1958) had done so previously.

The last time a player had any streak of four or more games with multiple rushing TDs no matter what point in the season was Hall of Famer LaDainian Tomlinson in his record-setting 2006 MVP season.

As for Rousseau, two sacks this week would make him the second player ever to log multiple QB takedowns in each of his team's first four games -- Hall of Famer Kevin Greene did it in 1998 with the Carolina Panthers. The only other player to do it in three straight games is Mark Gastineau, who had a then-record 22 sacks in 1984 with the New York Jets.

The only player this century with a streak of four or more games with multiple sacks at any point in a season was Simeon Rice on the Super Bowl champion 2002 Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

Rousseau's coaches and teammates attribute his early success to a variety of factors. New defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard transitioned the Bills from the 4-3 philosophy they ran under former coach Sean McDermott to a 3-4 base, allowing Rousseau to play from an upright position and create better angles to take advantage of his length and power.

Adding veteran Bradley Chubb in the offseason gives him a natural foil to draw attention away, and the emergence of second-year defensive tackle Deone Walker has a similar effect.

Mainly, though, Leonhard concedes Rousseau's just "on a heater." Dudes on hot streaks make plays. Rousseau's making plays. Chubb, for one, hopes the heater never fades. Leonhard admits offenses are going to try to scheme Rousseau out of his heater, but Rousseau's not particularly concerned about opponents paying him too much attention.

"You feel real good about yourself and then you get out there Sunday and that first play you see how fast the offense is moving and it's like 'Bruh, they're trying to win this game,'"

articles.headline: Is Brian Thomas Jr.'s playing time being impacted by an emerging Jaguars rookie?
articles.description: Thomas was targeted just once in Week 3. Will he rebound against the Bengals, or will other Jaguars pass catchers get all the work?
articles.headlineJa: ブライアン・トーマス・ジュニアのプレー時間は台頭するジャガーズの新人によって影響を受けているのか？
articles.descriptionJa: トーマスは第3週でわずか1回しかターゲットにされなかった。ベンガルズ戦で巻き返すのか、それともジャガーズの他のパスキャッチャーがすべての役割を担うことになるのか？
articles.body:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars have an emerging rookie receiver in Josh Cameron. But as Cameron sees more reps, is veteran receiver Brian Thomas Jr. getting the short end of the stick?

Cameron, a 2026 sixth-round pick, played as many snaps as Thomas and added a touchdown in last Sunday's win against the New England Patriots. It appears Cameron's role will continue to grow as the season continues when the Jaguars take on the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday (1 p.m. ET, CBS). But according to the team, that doesn't mean it will be at Thomas' expense. Coach Liam Coen said the Jaguars still have a plan for -- and definitely need -- the 2024 first-round pick.

"We need all these guys," Coen said. "... We are 100% going to need BT to make plays down the field and continue to ascend and make contested catches and do the things that he does really well. And that's on us as a staff to continue to put him in those positions, and he's going to make a ton of plays for us this year, I have no doubt in my mind."

Thomas and Cameron each played 23 snaps against the Patriots, a drop for Thomas from the 31 he played against the Denver Broncos one week earlier. Coen indicated the two drops Thomas had against the Broncos did not factor into that dip in play time. The Jaguars used more 12 personnel (one back, two tight ends) against the Broncos, and that allows only two receivers on the field. Still, Thomas was targeted just once -- the fewest times he has been targeted in a game in his career -- and caught an 8-yard pass. Cameron was targeted twice and had one catch, a 12-yard touchdown.

Thomas said this week that he's not worried about his dip in play time.

"I just say stay ready for when your opportunity comes," said Thomas, who has seven catches for 88 yards this season. "When you get your opportunity, just go out there and make the play."

Coen has said Thomas had an impressive offseason and the he was a major part of the offensive's push to go down the field more in 2026. In each of the first two games, he had three catches for 40 yards.

Cameron, meanwhile, has worked his way into a receiver rotation that includes Thomas, Jakobi Meyers and Parker Washington. To this point, Cameron has even had a bigger role than Travis Hunter (16 offensive snaps). His three catches for 32 yards in 2026 have been notable mostly because two have been for touchdowns. He has also had a significant role on all four special teams units -- sharing kickoff return duties with Ameer Abdullah and averaging 27.2 yards on five kickoff returns.

"He's really smart, first of all, just as a dude, as a person, but also football makes sense to him," Coen said. "To be able to handle the workload of not just the offensive game plan, but also the PP [personal protector] on punt, the kickoff dynamics that go into the kickoff coverage, and then also KOR. There's a lot that he does.

articles.headline: Kyler Murray's future with Vikings: Clock's already ticking
articles.description: Murray is on a one-year deal with a no-tag clause, so every game counts as both sides assess their future.
articles.headlineJa: カイラー・マレーのバイキングスでの未来：残された時間はすでに動き始めている
articles.descriptionJa: マレーはタグ禁止条項付きの1年契約を結んでおり、双方にとって将来を見極めるための毎試合が重要となる。
articles.body:
EAGAN, Minn. -- The Minnesota Vikings traded quarterback J.J. McCarthy on Monday, 886 days after they made him the No. 10 pick of the 2024 draft. He had played in only 10 games and thrown a total of 243 passes, a snippet in time that coach Kevin O'Connell found himself lamenting afterward. 

The Vikings had tried to identify what McCarthy's "truth and highest potential" was, O'Connell said, "within the timeline that's presented -- not the one that you necessarily would choose going into the whole thing."

To paraphrase baseball great Yogi Berra, it can get late early in the NFL when it comes time to make quarterback decisions. Circumstances don't always grant a generous window of time. It didn't exist for McCarthy, who joined a playoff-ready team when the Vikings drafted him, and it's not present for his successor, either. 

Kyler Murray is playing on a one-year contract with a no-franchise tag clause, meaning both he and the Vikings likely will have to render judgment on his long-term future over the next six months. They are already through 18% of the season, during which Murray has played one full game and 11 snaps of another, and the admittedly small sample size has provided no immediate evidence that he is a sure fit for the team. 

As the Vikings have started 3-0, Murray has completed 52.9% of his passes for 186 yards with one touchdown, two interceptions and four scrambles for 21 yards. Of the 38 quarterbacks who have started at least one game this season, his QBR (17.0) ranks No. 37. 

Both Murray and the Vikings have noted all of the obvious explanations -- Sunday's 23-16 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers was his first full game since October 2025, the Buccaneers' defense ranks No. 6 in EPA, he has played only three series with receiver Justin Jefferson -- while dismissing some of the subjective ones.

General manager Nolan Teasley noted this week, ahead of Sunday's game versus the Miami Dolphins (4:05 p.m. ET, Fox), the "potential" Murray has to succeed with the Vikings and said: "Still looking forward to that coming to fruition, and took some steps forward in that regard [in Tampa]."

Teasley added: "I'm excited about his trajectory in this offense."

The Vikings haven't had a quarterback who plays with Murray's multiplicity of skills in a long time, and it's clear that coaches and players are trying to adjust in real time. Right tackle Brian O'Neill noted there is "no more internal clock" for offensive linemen when they're pass blocking, given Murray's ability to move in the pocket and extend plays. It's a different style than the pocket passers the Vikings have employed in recent years, from Kirk Cousins to Sam Darnold, who were more likely to throw in the scheduled rhythm of a play.

"That's something we're going to have to get with," O'Neill said.

articles.headline: Patrick Mahomes, Chiefs have rediscovered the deep pass
articles.description: Much improved from last season, Mahomes has completed eight of 14 attempts on passes traveling at least 15 yards in 2026.
articles.headlineJa: パトリック・マホームズとチーフスがディープパスの威力を取り戻す
articles.descriptionJa: 昨シーズンから大きく改善し、マホームズは2026年に15ヤード以上のパスを14回中8回成功させている。
articles.body:
KANSAS CITY, Mo. -- In many ways, Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes made sizable improvements in his performance in September. Leading the Chiefs to a 3-0 record ahead of Sunday's matchup against the undefeated Las Vegas Raiders (4:25 p.m. ET, CBS), Mahomes has shown quality progress with his footwork, has been surgical when throwing play-action passes, and has been effective throwing the ball from outside of the pocket.

Not bad for a quarterback who returned to the field nine months after having surgery to repair the torn ACL and LCL in his left knee.

And yet, Mahomes' best trait this season has been throwing deep passes.

In fact, this season Mahomes has completed eight of 14 attempts in which the ball traveled at least 15 yards for 231 yards -- all of which have been recorded in the past two games.

"We'll have to continue to do that," Mahomes said Wednesday. "Obviously, we want to run the football, but if defenses are going to come up and try to stop the run, we have to be able to hit it over the top."

The Chiefs have been able to generate a large number of their deep completions through play-action passes, which has helped demonstrate the impact of running back Kenneth Walker III, who has produced 442 scrimmage yards. One of the best aspects for Mahomes is that he has been able to create highlights on deep throws with three different teammates -- tight end Travis Kelce and receivers Tyquan Thornton and Rashee Rice.

"With the play-action game, it's kind of opened up more things and made throws easier, more one-on-one type throws, so I give guys chances to make plays," Mahomes said. "We've had a lot of young receivers come in. I've gotten more and more reps with those guys, and it's hard to replicate reps under pressure in the game.

"I've gotten more and more comfortable throwing it to where they like to catch the football and then they go out there and just make the plays."

Mahomes struggled much of last season to connect with his pass catchers on deep passes. He completed only 42 of his 101 attempts in which the ball traveled at least 15 yards. His 41.6% completion percentage ranked 19th in the league. Mahomes also threw more interceptions (five) than he had touchdowns (two) on such throws.

The Chiefs' deep-passing attack should be tested in Sunday's game against the Raiders, who have created a league-high nine takeaways, including four interceptions.

If Mahomes wants to again have success downfield, the Chiefs will need to effectively block Raiders' pass rushers Maxx Crosby, Malcolm Koonce and Kwity Paye. The trio has collected a combined six sacks.

"He's one of the best competitors in the league," Mahomes said Wednesday of Crosby. That's where the respect comes from. We kind of have that mutual [desire] to be the best on the field when we're out there. It brings out the best in you."

articles.headline: Have the Rams improved special teams enough to make a difference?
articles.description: The Rams will get a chance to see how effective such changes have been when they travel to Philly this weekend.
articles.headlineJa: ラムズは勝敗を左右するほどスペシャルチームを改善できたのか？
articles.descriptionJa: 今週末にフィラデルフィアに遠征するラムズは、こうした変更がどれほど効果的であったかを確認する機会を得る。
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES -- It was Week 3 of the 2025 season -- nearly a year ago -- and the Rams were on their way to a 3-0 start for the first time since 2021.

But after leading the Philadelphia Eagles 26-7 early in the third quarter, the Rams imploded. Along with not scoring another point on offense, the Rams had two field goals blocked in the fourth quarter, including one on the final play of the game that was returned 61 yards for a touchdown that gave the Eagles a 33-26 victory.

"That seemed like a crazier one," Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford said when asked whether he's ever experienced an ending to a game like that. "Obviously, we played well in the first half of that game. We had some opportunities to distance ourselves and didn't do that for one reason or another. Then they made some great plays on special teams."

That loss to the Eagles was the first big crack to show in a unit that struggled for most of last season. Although the Rams were 11-4 through Week 16, Los Angeles fired its special teams coordinator after a loss to the eventual Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks. Earlier in the season, the Rams had replaced their long snapper and kicker after the unit continued to have issues throughout the season, missing field goals and extra points.

Their new kicker, Harrison Mevis, was 12-of-13 on field goals and 39-of-39 on extra points to finish the regular season. He did not miss a kick during the playoffs.

More changes came this offseason, when the Rams hired Bubba Ventrone as their special teams coordinator. The Rams will get a chance to see how effective these changes have been when they travel to Philadelphia to play the Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field on Sunday (1 p.m. ET, FOX). Through three games, the Rams rank last in special teams DVOA and are ranked 30th, according to ESPN Analytics, ahead of only the Dolphins and Titans. 

During training camp, coach Sean McVay said it has been a focus to not overlook the phase, but instead show how "important" and "impactful" the unit is.

"I'm not going to run away [from the fact] that I haven't done a good enough job of making that an emphasis, and it's cost us," McVay said. "And that is nobody's fault but my own."

Now, a year later, McVay is asked whether he thinks the special teams unit is in a better position than it was last season.

"Yeah, I do and that particular phase, without a doubt," McVay said. "... That particular operation I thought was a major step in the right direction, especially Mevis going 4-of-4 and 2-of-2 on the extra points [against the Denver Broncos in Week 3]. But you have to do it again."

Mevis said he's felt the "change of culture" since Ventrone was hired by the Rams.

"Special teams is at a premium all across the board," Mevis said of the emphasis this season. "I think obviously there's been past games I think that have been influenced on special teams, and we've seen how it influences games. So it's at the top of the list for us. We're pushing for good specia

articles.headline: FA: Man City verdict has 'significant implications for integrity of game'
articles.description: The Football Association have expressed their concern that the guilty charge aimed at Manchester City over the Premier League's financial rules stains the "integrity" of the game.
articles.headlineJa: FA：マンチェスター・シティ裁定は「競技の公平性に重大な影響を及ぼす」
articles.descriptionJa: イングランドサッカー協会（FA）は、プレミアリーグの財務ルール違反を巡るマンチェスター・シティへの有罪判定が競技の「公平性」を損なうとして懸念を表明しました。
articles.body:
The Football Association have expressed their concern that the guilty charge aimed at Manchester City over the Premier League's financial rules stains the "integrity" of the game.

The FA's full statement read: "The Independent Commission's decision has significant implications for the integrity of the game. We are carefully considering the decision and its implications and will take action where appropriate.

"As proceedings between the Premier League and Manchester City Football Club remain ongoing, we do not intend to comment further at this stage. We will, however, continue to monitor developments closely."

Friday, Oct. 2 is the deadline for City to appeal the guilty verdict into their breaches of Premier League rules. They have stated that they intend to appeal.

The commission concluded more than £830 million ($1.1 bn) of such funding was used to inflate revenues and enable the club to comply with Premier League and UEFA financial rules through a series of "sham" arrangements.

At the heart of the club's appeal will be an insistence that government funding, provided via the Abu Dhabi Crown Prince Court (CPC), gave financial assistance to sponsors in the emirate to help them to fulfil their liabilities to City, rather than Sheikh Mansour's Abu Dhabi United Group (ADUG) company, which owns the club.

The 40-page core decision published on Tuesday shows the independent commission rejected the CPC explanation as "untrue" in its findings, adding: "We concluded that it was an 'explanation' that the club had concocted well after the event in an attempt to obscure and conceal the realities of the disguised funding scheme."

Sponsor Etihad Airways, which is owned by an Abu Dhabi fund chaired by City owner Sheikh Mansour's brother, is considering legal action against the Premier League.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham told the BBC earlier this week that he would be concerned if City's owners sold the club due to the guilty verdict because they have been "a huge partner in the building of modern Manchester." But a No. 10 Downing Street spokesman afterwards: "As the Prime Minister made clear, the initial judgement is serious and there can't be any suggestion that anyone is above the rules.

"He also stressed that it is an ongoing independent process. It is essential that it is allowed to run its course and the outcome respected.

"If wrongdoing is established, those responsible should face the appropriate consequences."

But Jamie Carragher wrote for The Telegraph: "The club can only heal and recover from the shame of their guilt once the custodians recognise they have failed in their duty and sell up."

articles.headline: Sir Alex Ferguson was 'terrified' about Old Trafford return after brain surgery
articles.description: Sir Alex Ferguson has revealed he was "terrified" when returning to Old Trafford for the first time following brain surgery in 2018.
articles.headlineJa: アレックス・ファーガソン卿、脳手術後のオールド・トラッフォード復帰に「恐怖を感じていた」
articles.descriptionJa: アレックス・ファーガソン卿は、2018年に脳手術を受けてから初めてオールド・トラッフォードへ復帰した際、「恐怖を感じていた」と明かしました。
articles.body:
Sir Alex Ferguson has revealed he was "terrified" when returning to Old Trafford for the first time following brain surgery in 2018.

The former Manchester United manager, now 84, suffered a brain haemorrhage at the age of 76 and returned to the stadium four months later to watch them play Wolves in the Premier League.

"I was terrified actually," Ferguson told BBC Breakfast. "I wish I could say I was comfortable. I wasn't."

Ferguson and late wife Cathy were given a standing ovation when taking their seats in the directors' box.

"My wife was with me, and she was nearly crying," Ferguson said. "When we sat down, she said, 'that's fantastic.'"

Ferguson had retired as United boss five years before his brain haemorrhage, having won 36 major trophies during his 26-year spell in charge.

He also spoke about his fear after being left unable to talk in the days following his surgery.

"I had lost my voice. I couldn't speak," he said. "That was a frightening moment. I remember my grandsons coming to see me and I had lost my voice.

"Then they brought in a therapist and she started doing things like asking me to write down the names of birds, names of animals, names of rivers. That way my voice came back."

- Portugal, Man United, Real Madrid: Cristiano Ronaldo's long history of rows with coaches

- Transfer rumors, news: Man United, Chelsea monitoring Benfica defender

- FA charges Fulham boss Álvaro Arbeloa with misconduct for comments after Man United draw

When asked about his health now, he added: "I'm feeling quite good despite small injuries."

Ferguson has a new book in the pipeline, 'Games of My Life', in which he recalls the 21 matches he feels defined his career.

His unrivalled trophy haul at Old Trafford included 13 Premier League titles, two Champions Leagues, five FA Cups, four League Cups and the European Cup Winners' Cup.

articles.headline: 2026 Ballon d'Or: Full men's, women's short lists, host city change, more
articles.description: The 2026 Ballon d'Or short lists are out. Here's who could win the biggest individual prizes in men's and women's soccer.
articles.headlineJa: 2026年バロンドール：男女の最終候補全リスト、開催都市の変更など
articles.descriptionJa: 2026年バロンドールの最終候補リストが発表されました。男女サッカー界における最高の個人賞を獲得する可能性がある候補者たちを紹介します。
articles.body:
It's nearly that time again.

The 2026 Ballon d'Or awards -- the annual ceremony in which France Football Magazine crowns the best men's and women's players in the world -- are fast approaching, with the short list for each award announced on Tuesday.

The Ballon d'Or trophies are handed out based on the criteria of: "1) Individual performances, decisive and impressive character, 2) Team performances and achievements, 3) Class and fair play."

Any player in world football is eligible, no matter the league they play in or their country of origin, and the short lists are decided by a jury of 100 journalists from around the world. So who is nominated for this year's awards, and who could win?

When is the 2026 Ballon d'Or ceremony, and why isn't it in Paris?

The 2026 Ballon d'Or awards, which have long been presented by France Football Magazine, will be handed out on Oct. 26. There will be a difference this year, though: The star-studded ceremony will not take place in Paris. Instead, it will be held in London at The London Palladium theater to mark the gala's 70th anniversary.

The first Ballon d'Or ceremony was a much more humble affair, held in Blackpool, England, and awarded to 41-year-old star forward Stanley Matthews.

Matthews was an all-time England great who spent the majority of his career at Blackpool and Stoke City and, when announcing the venue change, was described by organizers as a "true ambassador of football."

"As the Ballon d'Or becomes of septuagenarian age, it is fitting in such a landmark year to celebrate the finest present-day exponents of the beautiful game in the beating heart of the country that first conceived of it," organizers added.

Full 30-player Ballon d'Or short list

Jude Bellingham

Club: Real Madrid

Country: England

Bellingham didn't win a trophy with Real Madrid for the second year running, but the all-action midfielder was an important pillar of England's bronze medal-winning display at the 2026 World Cup. The 23-year-old scored seven goals at the tournament and his virtuoso two-goal display against Mexico in the round of 16 is likely to go down in Three Lions' folklore.

 Pau Cubarsí

Club: Barcelona

Country: Spain

A debut nomination for 19-year-old center back Cubarsi, who played an important role in Barcelona's 2025-26 title win before being crowned Best Young Player at the World Cup after playing every single minute of Spain's monumental victory, keeping seven clean sheets along the way. He is also nominated for the Kopa Trophy, which is awarded to the best player aged 21 or younger.

 Marc Cucurella

Club: Chelsea / Real Madrid

Country: Spain

Cucurella was a mainstay for Chelsea in the Premier League in 2025-26 before completing a transfer to Real Madrid during the World Cup. The energetic left back played every single minute for Spain at the tournament, and even provided two assists before ending his summer as a world champion.

Club: Paris Saint-Germain

Country: France

articles.headline: Watson leads third straight winning drive, puts Browns atop North
articles.description: Deshaun Watson has the Browns atop the division at 3-1 after directing a winning drive for the third straight game Thursday night in a 27-24 win over the Steelers.
articles.headlineJa: ワトソンが3試合連続の決勝ドライブを導き、ブラウンズを北地区首位に押し上げる
articles.descriptionJa: デショーン・ワトソンが木曜夜に行われたスティーラーズ戦（27-24）で3試合連続となる決勝ドライブを指揮し、ブラウンズを3勝1敗で地区首位に立たせた。
articles.body:
CLEVELAND -- For the third consecutive game, quarterback Deshaun Watson led a winning drive for the Cleveland Browns.

Four days after he threw for the winning score in Cleveland's Week 3 home win over the Carolina Panthers, Watson led the Browns on another late-game drive. This time, he put the Browns in range for Andre Szmyt's 56-yard field goal with 10 seconds left as Cleveland defeated the Pittsburgh Steelers 27-24 on Thursday night.

Watson joined Brian Sipe as the second Browns quarterback since the 1970 merger to lead a winning drive in the fourth quarter or overtime of three straight games, according to ESPN Research.

"It was electric. It was amazing," Watson said. "From the time we came out pregame, it was super dope to be called out, hear the crowd and feel the energy. From start to finish, the crowd was in it, the energy of the stadium, we fed off them. To get a big victory against a divisional rival on primetime, this [is] what you dream about. This is what you work for. These are the things that you put that grind in during the summertime and training camp for nights like this. It was amazing."

The victory, Cleveland's third straight after a 24-point road loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 1, gave the Browns their first 3-1 start since 2021 and moved them into sole possession of the AFC North for the first time since Nov. 9, 2014.

Late turnarounds after slow starts defined Watson's previous two winning drives. But on Thursday night, Watson had one of his best first halves in a Browns uniform. Watson threw for 181 yards, his most in the first half of a game in Cleveland, as the offense scored touchdowns on three consecutive drives in the second quarter. The Browns led 21-10 at halftime, and their 21 points in the second quarter were their most in any quarter of a game since the 2020 wild-card round, also against the Steelers.

The offense stalled for much of the second half, though, and a pair of turnovers from Watson played a role in Pittsburgh being able to erase the deficit. He was stripped in the third quarter by edge rusher T.J. Watt on a rush attempt, and the Steelers recovered. Watson was also intercepted early in the fourth quarter on a pass that was tipped. Pittsburgh scored a touchdown after the giveaway but failed on the 2-point attempt, cutting the Browns' lead to 21-16 with 10:10 remaining.

The Steelers tied the score at 24-24 on a 3-yard touchdown pass from Aaron Rodgers to tight end Pat Freiermuth and a successful 2-point try on a 1-yard sneak by Rodgers after defensive end Jared Verse was flagged for being offsides.

Watson, though, quickly drove the Browns down the field with four straight completions. He was sacked for a 4-yard loss two plays before the winning kick, but he was already within Szmyt's range.

Safety Grant Delpit intercepted a desperation heave from Rodgers to preserve the victory.

articles.body:

Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Manchester United and Chelsea are monitoring a deal for Benfica defender Tomás Araújo, according to TEAMTalk. The 24-year-old is claimed to be on the radar of several Premier League clubs, but it's United and Chelsea who are most keen. Araujo, who can play center back and right-back, recently signed a contract extension until 2031, making an exit in January unlikely. However, with a release clause valued at £68 million, clubs could pursue a switch anyway

- Jadon Sancho is willing to hold out until January as a free agent before making a decision, if the right offer doesn't arrive before then, reports TEAMtalk. The former Manchester United and Borussia Dortmund winger is a free agent, following his exit from Old Trafford at the end of his contract in the summer. The 26-year-old has been linked with a whole host of clubs since, but is yet to make a decision on his future, with nothing advanced on his next club.

- Juventus are preparing a huge rebuild over the next year, with Tuttosport naming a whole host of potential transfer targets for the Italian club. In the goalkeeping ranks, Alisson Becker is claimed to be a player of interest, as he could leave Liverpool at the end of the season as a free agent. In defence, Oumar Solet of Udinese is viewed as an option, while RB Leipzig ace David Raum and Crystal Palace star Tyrick Mitchell are also on the Bianconeri's radar. Napoli stalwart Stanislav Lobotka, Manchester City midfielder Mateo Kovacic, and Real Madrid playmaker Brahim Díaz are touted as options for the central ranks. Meanwhile, Crystal Palace forward Jean-Philippe Mateta could be a striker arrival.

- João Félix is keen on making a return to Barcelona next year, when the Portuguese international's contract with Al Nassr is set to expire. That's according to Sport, which reports that the 27-year-old has his sights set on a return to the Champions League after a recent resurgence in his career in the Saudi Pro League. Felix previously spent a year on loan with Barcelona from Atletico Madrid, where he made 44 appearances with 10 goals and six assists. Now back in form, and eyeing a possible free transfer, a return to the Nou Camp is on his mind, though the report claims that he is not viewed as a priority target.

- Juventus have declared that Kenan Yildiz and Kerim Alajbegovic are "untouchable" in future transfer markets, with the club keen to build around the pair, reports La Gazzetta.
